title: docs(adr): ADR-0140 — v18 is the first LTS line, `latest` follows it, breaking changes batch into quarterly majors
body:
## What

Records the maintainer's 2026-10-24 in-session ruling — 「接受 18.x 作为 LTS 并放慢破坏性变更」 — as **ADR-0140 (Proposed)** and amends the 「阶段姿态」 paragraph of `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` to match. The record declares; it implements nothing. Execution cards (branch cut, `release.yml` lanes, the `LTS Changeset Gate`, the backport workflow, pre mode on `main`, docs, objectui mirror, cloud record) are listed in the ADR and are cut only after acceptance.

## The decision, in one table

| | `main` | `release/18.x` (LTS) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Takes | everything, at today's speed | fixes only, by a closed list (D2): security, data integrity, regressions, docs, advisory dep bumps, console pin along objectui's 18.x |
| Publishes to | `next` (`19.0.0-next.N`, pre mode) | `latest` + `lts-18`, patch releases |
| Breaking changes | allowed; graded per the #25105 ruling; reach `latest` only as a major, **at most once a quarter**, with the ADR-0087 chain complete (D5) | never, except a `LTS-exception: security \| data-integrity` fail-closed fix (D2) |
| How changes arrive | PRs as today | main-first, then `backport:18.x` label → fleet-opened cherry-pick PR → same required set + `LTS Changeset Gate` (D3) |
| Window | — | 12 months from 18.0.0 GA (until 2027-10-20) or 3 months after the next LTS GA, whichever is later (D1, D9) |

Also: one LTS line at a time, never a third line (sized to the team recorded in the ADR header); `npm create objectstack@latest` scaffolds the LTS line (D6); objectui mirrors the branch and the LTS console pin moves only along it (D7); the commercial promise is the cloud half (D8, Provenance).

## Why

Seventeen majors in nine months and, since 18.0.0, a `patch` that may carry a non-protocol breaking change (18.1.0: 90 changesets declared breaking, 42 graded `patch`). That posture was right with no one standing under it. There are now paying enterprise deployments and partners who need a line that does not move under them, while the open-source framework and the cloud keep their speed for developers worldwide. The ADR keeps `main` fast and gives customers a line to stand on.

## Scope and governance

- Files: `docs/adr/0140-long-term-support-lines.md` (new), `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` (one paragraph).
- Both paths are **Tier H governed surfaces** (Prime Directive #14): this PR stays a draft and lands only on the maintainer's approval — no seat merges, queues or arms auto-merge on it.
- Publishes nothing from any released package: no changeset. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- `node scripts/check-adr-links.mjs` passes (776 relative link destinations resolve).
- Branch name follows this session's designated branch rather than the `claude/issue-<n>-<slug>` convention; there is no card, since the ruling was given directly by the maintainer in session.

## Review focus

1. D1 window length and the D5 quarterly cadence (first candidate 19.0.0, first week of 2027-01) — both are judgement calls the maintainer may want to change.
2. D4: `latest` follows the LTS line while `main` publishes to `next`. The alternative (Node-style, `latest` = trunk) is rejected in the ADR because a `main` patch may be breaking under #25105.
3. D2's closed list and the single named exception.
